Results.title: Apps Like Pinterest for Kids: Safer Ways to Find Creative Ideas - Taroo
Results.content:
DIY.org is built around the idea that children learn through making. Its current platform includes creative challenges, tools for making games and digital projects, and a community where children can share what they create. DIY says its experience is designed for ages 5–15, with moderated communities, no ads, and parent controls.

For children who like a clear challenge and a project to complete, that can be much more actionable than scrolling through visual inspiration. [...] Scratch combines a creation tool with a huge community of projects made by other users.

Children can explore games, animations, stories, and experiments, then make or remix projects of their own. Scratch is primarily designed for ages 8–16 and is maintained by the MIT Media Lab's Lifelong Kindergarten group.

This makes it particularly powerful for kids who learn by seeing something interesting and wondering:

How did they make that?

Why parents may like it: [...] Others already know what they like and want to explore: Show me more drawing ideas, LEGO builds, crafts, or animals.

For kids who need inspiration and somewhere to turn it into something of their own, Taroo is our top pick. Kids can choose from a large library of creative quests across stories, drawing, music, speaking, and observation, take part in weekly challenges inspired by other kids' creations, and use AI as a co-creator to develop and improve their ideas.

Results.content:
| Design strength | What it looks like |

| Ideation | Prompts, challenges, or tools that help kids decide what to make |
| Making | Turning an idea into a story, object, room, game, image, or world |
| Choice | Kids decide how the creation looks, behaves, or develops |
| Iteration | Easy ways to change, test, rebuild, or improve |
| Problem-solving | Working within space, logic, materials, rules, or other constraints |
| Ownership | A finished creation kids can explain or show someone | [...] Taroo is a strong choice for broad guided creativity. Tinkercad is excellent for 3D objects, Scratch for interactive projects, Canva for visual design, and Minecraft Creative for world-building.

### What is the best free design app for kids?

Scratch and Tinkercad are two strong free options. Scratch focuses on games and interactive experiences, while Tinkercad focuses on 3D objects and inventions.

### What is the best design app for a 7-year-old? [...] Professional design tools become powerful once a child already has an idea.

Taroo focuses more on helping that idea emerge and develop.

Kids get creative quests across several mediums, make their own choices, and can co-create with AI when they need another possibility or feedback on where to go next.

It is not a replacement for Tinkercad, Scratch, Minecraft, or Canva.

Results.title: Is Toca Boca Educational? What Kids Learn From Pretend Play - Taroo
Results.content:
### What app pairs well with Toca Boca?

Taroo pairs well with Toca Boca for kids ages 6–10 because it adds short creative quests across storytelling, drawing, rhythm, observation, and expression. It gives children more structured ways to turn imagination into creative output.

## You may also like

###### The Sound Detective Game: A Listening Activity for Kids

###### The “What If?” Story Game: A Simple Creative Writing Activity for Kids

###### Best Museums for Young Children in the U.S. [...] In Toca Boca, a child may create a scene and decide what happens. In Taroo, a child may get a specific creative starting point: describe this image, continue this story, complete this drawing, make this rhythm, or go on a photo quest.

That makes Taroo useful for kids ages 6–10 who enjoy imagination but need a little more structure. It is not about replacing pretend play. It is about expanding the creative muscles around it. [...] It also contains in-app purchases. Toca Boca’s support page says the app is free to download and includes in-app purchases, so parents should be aware that the full experience may involve paid content.

So the best answer is balanced: Toca Boca can be educational, but it is not automatically enough.

It is pretend play. Pretend play is valuable. But children also benefit from prompts, conversation, creative output, and chances to explain their ideas.
